rv.q: “Meet Vera Stark” sheds a witty, wince-inducing light on artists determined to shine regardless of the race-based barriers.
It’s an often funny and absorbing performance that anchors a Nottage play that, like the fictional Vera Stark, deserves another look.
I recommend it with reservations. They really have to get the technical problems in order.
As bizarre and choppy as Act I seems, Act II simply becomes tiresome and redundant, until it finally runs out of steam by the end.

While I was quite impressed with the first act and the quality of the performances by all six of the cast members, I felt that the second act was somewhat tedious and probably brought to much to the table.

cn.t: Nottage's satirical look at race in 1930s Hollywood earns mixed reviews. Critics praise the playwright's sharp examination of Black actors' struggles, but some find the production overlong and uneven in execution.
